newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks head into the weekend sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: German stocks head into the weekend sharply lower.

text.p: German shares ended late trade lower on Friday, with the market still suffering from an overnight correction on Wall Street and with no new good news evident in early trade across the Atlantic to lift the market.
The IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, ended at 2,982.63 points, down 54.65 points or 1.80 percent, well shy of the psychologically-key 3,000-point level.
The market seemed unable to convincingly penetrate that threshold and forge further gains, but dealers said this was not yet its long-awaited correction.
"We would welcome a bit of a breather in this market after the last couple of weeks, but we are mostly looking to new data next week to decide where we'll go," said one Frankfurt trader.
Earlier, the DAX-30 index ended at 2,998.24 points, down 35.22 points or 1.16 percent, after the Dow Jones index closed sharply lower overnight.
Wall Street had finished lower on a wave of "programme" selling, where computers have been programmed to initiate sell orders once a certain set of conditions have been fulfilled.
The Dow Jones Industrial Index opened slightly lower on Friday.
Support for German shares came from the dollar at 1.62 marks, off the highs of earlier in the week, but still stable enough to underpin trade.
Traders said that many shares saw a lot of volatility over the day, including industrial group Mannesmann AG, which ended down 10.90 marks at 642.25 marks.

Focus was also on the banking sector, which has been in favour of late, especially Bayerische Hypotheken-und Wechselbank AG. Hypo-Bank ended up 1.15 marks, or 2.18 percent, at 53.80 marks, amid unconfirmed speculation that it was trying to dispose of some of its industrial holdings.

Next week's corporate events include a full annual results news conference at Thyssen AG in Duesseldorf on Monday, and dealers said they were expecting positive developments in Thyssen's earnings per share for 1996.
